rows.speaker: أبو يزيد المدني
rows.claim: Abu Jahl acknowledged Muhammad’s truth after a handshake, but said he could not follow a man from Banu Abd Manaf; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد المدني: لقي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا جهل فصافحه

rows.speaker: ناجية بن كعب
rows.claim: Najiya reports Abu Jahl saying he did not accuse Muhammad of lying, but rejected the message he brought; the verse followed.
rows.anchor: وقال ناجية بن كعب: قال أبو جهل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما نتهمك ولا نكذبك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil identifies al-Harith ibn Amir: he privately believed Muhammad truthful but feared Arab retaliation and loss of security if he followed him.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في الحرث بن عامر بن نوفل بن عبد مناف بن قصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, al-Kisa'i, and Ali read يُكذِّبونك lightly: the people do not find Muhammad to be a liar.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع والكسائي: يكذبونك بالتخفيف وهي قراءة علي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i distinguishes forms: أكذبت means reporting that someone spoke falsely, while كذبت means judging that person a liar.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: يقول العرب: أكذبت الرسل إذا أخبرت إنه قول الكذب

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba’s line uses أهيج to mean that one found the land producing vegetation, supporting the light-reading’s idiom.
rows.anchor: قال رؤبة: وأهيج الخلصاء من ذات البرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers deny God’s signs even though they know the Prophet is truthful.
rows.anchor: ولكن الظالمين بآيات الله يجحدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were called liars and endured denial and injury until God’s help came, consoling Muhammad to persevere.
rows.anchor: فصبروا على ما كذبوا وأوذوا حتى أتاهم نصرنا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God’s unchangeable words here mean the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ولا مبدل لكلمات الله قال الكلبي: يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the unchangeable words with God’s prior promise of victory for His messengers and believers.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: يعني قوله ولقد سبقت كلمتنا ولا مبدل لكلمات الله إلى قوله: غالبون

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima also links the promise to God’s pledge to help messengers and believers in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقوله: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima also cites God’s decree that He and His messengers will prevail.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى كتب الله لأغلبن أنا ورسلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about earlier messengers means that reports of messengers’ experiences had already reached Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ولقد جاءك من نبإ المرسلين من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression أصابنا من مطر أي مطر is an idiom meaning that rain struck them, illustrating the phrasing of a report.
rows.anchor: كما يقول: أصابنا من مطر أي مطر

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق، والضحاك، والكلبي
rows.claim: They say Azar was Ibrahim’s father, like Israel is another name for Jacob, and that he came from Kutha near Kufa.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق والضحاك والكلبي: وآزر أبو إبراهيم وهو تاريخ مثل إسرائيل ويعقوب

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Maqatil ibn Hayyan says Azar was Ibrahim’s paternal uncle.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: لأب إبراهيم

rows.speaker: سليمان التيمي
rows.claim: Sulayman al-Taymi takes Azar as an insult meaning crooked; another gloss in the passage gives a Persian term for an old man.
rows.anchor: وقال سليمان [التيمي] : هو سب وعيب. ومعناه في كلامهم المعوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the insult or Persian-word interpretations, Azar is genitive as an appositive or adjective but appears accusative because it is indeclinable.
rows.anchor: وهو على هذه الأقاويل في محل الخفض على البدل أو الصفحة ولكنه نصب لأنه لا ينصرف

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب، ومجاهد، ويمان
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, and Yaman say Azar was the name of an idol, making it accusative.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب، ومجاهد، ويمان: آزر اسم صنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word order is advanced: the sense is, ‘Do you take Azar’s idols as gods?’
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام تقديم وتأخير تقديره أتتخذ آزر أصناما آلهة

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو يزيد المدني ويعقوب الحضرمي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce Azar nominative as a singular vocative: ‘O Azar, do you take idols as gods?’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو يزيد المدني ويعقوب الحضرمي: آزر بالرفع على النداء بالمفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Ibrahim the kingdom of heaven and earth as He had shown him insight into religion and the truth against his people; الملكوت means sovereignty.
rows.anchor: يعني كما أريناه البصيرة في دينه والحق في خلاف قومه نريه ملكوت السماوات والأرض أي ملكهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suffix in ملكوت is an added feminine marker, as in جبروت، رهبوت، and رحموت.
rows.anchor: والملكوت الملك وبدت فيه وجدت التاء للتأنيث في الجبروت والرهبوت والرحموت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Nimrod dreamed a star extinguished the sun and moon; diviners predicted a boy would destroy his rule, so he ordered newborn boys killed and men separated from women; Azar then conceived Ibrahim with his wife.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: رأى نمرود في منامه كأن كوكبا اطلع فذهب بضوء الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Nimrod detained every pregnant woman in town except Ibrahim’s mother, whose youth kept her from recognizing pregnancy.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: بعث النمرود إلى كل امرأة حبلى بقريته فحبسها عنده

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Nimrod sent men away and made trusted Azar swear not to approach his wife; Azar returned, saw her, and could not restrain himself, causing the pregnancy.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: خرج نمرود بالرجال إلى المعسكر ونحاهم عن النساء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says diviners alerted Nimrod to the pregnancy; Ibrahim’s mother fled during labor, hid the newborn by a dry river, and Azar concealed him in a sealed burrow where his mother nursed him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما حملت أم إبراهيم، قالت الكهان لنمرود: إن الغلام الذي أخبرناك به

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi places the birth in an underground chamber near Kufa and Basra; Ibrahim grew unusually fast, appearing three at one year, so Azar eventually presented his grown son to his companions.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: لما أعظم بطن أم إبراهيم خشي آزر أن يذبح فانطلق بها إلى أرض بين الكوفة والبصرة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Ibrahim’s mother gave birth in a nearby cave, sealed him inside, and later found him alive sucking his thumb.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: لما وجدت أم إبراهيم الطلق خرجت ليلا إلى مغارة

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq says Ibrahim sucked water, honey, milk, dates, and clarified butter from five different fingers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو روق: كانت أم إبراهيم كلما دخلت على إبراهيم وجدته يمص أصابعه

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Azar believed the mother’s claim that the baby had died; Ibrahim aged a day each month and left the cave after fifteen months.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: وكان آزر قد سأل أم إبراهيم عن حملها ما فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the reported dialogue, Ibrahim asks who created his mother, father, and Nimrod; after Azar slaps him, Ibrahim asks to leave the burrow.
rows.anchor: قال لأبويه: أخرجاني، فأخرجاه من السرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing livestock, Ibrahim reasons that they must have a Lord and Creator, then identifies the Creator who provides for him as his only Lord.
rows.anchor: ما لهذه بد من أن يكن لها رب وخالق ثم نظر وتفكر في خلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Ibrahim first saw Jupiter, or Venus, before the moon late in the month and called the star his lord.
rows.anchor: وإنما سميت الجن لاجتنانها فلا ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جن عليه الليل means night fell and became dark; related forms mean to cover or grow dark, and jinn are named for being hidden from sight.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله عز وجل: فلما جن عليه الليل أي دخل يقال: جن الليل وأجن وجنه الليل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses جنون الليل as its darkness and cites a line about night sheltering a ride; no poet is named in the passage.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: جنون الليل سواده، وأنشد: فلولا جنان الليل أدرك ركضنا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view takes Ibrahim’s statements at face value: he was a child before proof and guidance, when he was neither an unbeliever nor a believer.
rows.anchor: فأجراه بعضهم على الظاهر. وقالوا: ما كان إبراهيم (عليه السلام) مسترشدا متحيرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through Ali ibn Abi Talha, Ibn Abbas says Ibrahim worshipped the star, moon, and sun until each set, then asked for guidance and disavowed shirk.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه ما روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال: لما جن عليه الليل رأى كوكبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other scholars reject that account because a prophet cannot pass through a time without monotheism, knowledge, or disavowal of every other object of worship.
rows.anchor: وأنكر الآخرون هذا القول، وقالوا: غير جائز أن يكون لله عز وجل رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They argue Ibrahim already had divinely granted right guidance and a pure heart, and had been shown the kingdom of heaven and earth; literal belief in a star as God is impossible.
rows.anchor: وأراه ملكوته فقال: إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم وقال وكذلك نري إبراهيم ملكوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first of four interpretations is that Ibrahim feigned agreement with star-worshippers to expose their error: setting revealed the celestial bodies’ incapacity, although his people revered and consulted them.
rows.anchor: الوجه الأول: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) أراد أن يستدرجهم بهذا القول ويعرفهم خطأهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An analogy begins with a visitor to idol-worshippers who feigned reverence for their idol to gain their confidence and later expose their error.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا مثل الجواري الذي ورد على قوم يعبدون بدا لهم وهو الصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation treats ‘this is my lord’ as an argument from the opponents’ own assumptions: the star sets, and the moon is greater, so their worship is untenable.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثالث: أن إبراهيم (عليه السلام) قال هذا على وجه الاحتجاج على قومه لا على معنى الشك في ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account uses ellipsis: Ibrahim means ‘they say this is my lord’; as with the prayer after Abraham and Ishmael raised the House’s foundations.
rows.anchor: في الآية اختصار وإضمار ومعناها قال: يقولون هذا ربي كقوله وإذ يرفع إبراهيم القواعد من البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim rejects a lord that disappears at setting, then repeats the argument for the moon and sun; the sun’s greater brightness makes its disappearance still clearer.
rows.anchor: فلما أفل غاب وزال قال: لا أحب الآفلين ربا، لا يدوم

rows.speaker: محمد بن مقاتل الرازي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Muqatil explains the masculine هذا: Ibrahim saw the sun’s light or ray, not the sun’s disk.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن مقاتل الرازي: إنما قال هذا ولم يقل هذه لأنه رأى ضوء الشمس

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses هذا as ‘this rising one’ or ‘this arriving one’; the sun was larger and brighter, and its setting prompted Ibrahim’s disavowal.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: أراد هذا الطالع ربي أو هذا الآتي أراه ربي هذا أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azar made idols and gave them to Ibrahim to sell; Ibrahim called them harmful and useless, then mocked them by putting their heads in a river and telling them to drink.
rows.anchor: وكان آزر يصنع الأصنام فلما ضم إبراهيم إلى نفسه جعل يصنع الأصنام ويعطيها إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حاجه means his people argued with him; Ibrahim says God has guided him to monotheism and truth, so their debate cannot undo that guidance.
rows.anchor: وحاجه أي خاصمه قومه في دينه قال لهم أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان عرفني التوحيد والحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim’s people warned that their idols might afflict him with leprosy or madness for insulting them; he says he fears them only if his Lord wills.
rows.anchor: وذلك إنهم قالوا له: أما تخاف أن تمسك آلهتنا بسوء من برص أو خبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s knowledge encompasses everything, so Ibrahim asks whether the people will remember that the idols are subject to His will.
rows.anchor: وسع ربي كل شيء علما يعني أحاط علمه بكل شيء أفلا تتذكرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim says the idols neither see, hear, harm, nor benefit; his opponents should fear associating with God a partner for which they have no revealed proof.
rows.anchor: يعني الأصنام وهي لا تبصر ولا تسمع ولا تضر ولا تنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim asks which side deserves security; God judges that those who believe without mixing faith with shirk have security and guidance.
rows.anchor: فقال الله عز وجل قاضيا وحاكما بينهما الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Come, I will recite’ means Muhammad is to proclaim with certainty what God truly forbade, as revelation and command, not speculation or denial.
rows.anchor: ثم قال قل يا محمد تعالوا أتل أقرأ ما حرم ربكم عليكم حقا يقينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians differ on the case and construction of ألا تشركوا: it can complete حرم with an extra لا, or mean ‘that you do not associate’, or depend on أوحى.
rows.anchor: اختلفوا في محل أن فقال بعضهم: [محله] نصب، ثم اختلفوا في وجه انتصابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses make ألا تشركوا an apposition to what God forbade, or place a break after حرم ربكم and read عليكم أن لا تشركوا.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أوحى ألا تشركوا، وقيل: [ما] بدل [من] ما حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also discusses whether later prohibitions coordinate in the accusative or take a jussive construction, citing a command followed by a prohibition and poetry as grammatical evidence.
rows.anchor: ولا تكونن من المشركين عطف بالنهي على الخبر قال الشاعر: حج وأوصي بسليمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on killing children addresses burying daughters for fear of poverty: God provides for the parents and their children; إملَاق means poverty or depleted provisions.
rows.anchor: والإملاق الفقر ونفاد الزاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparent indecencies are public acts and hidden ones are private acts; pre-Islamic people condemned public adultery but tolerated it in secret, so both are forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: كانوا في الجاهلية يستقبحون الزنا في العلانية ولا يرون به بأسا في السر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the apparent indecency as wine; the excerpt’s gloss of the hidden one is truncated.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ما ظهر الخمر وما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protected life is that of a believer or treaty-holder; lawful exceptions are apostasy, retaliation for murder, and stoning for adultery after marriage.
rows.anchor: يعني بما أباح قبلها وهي الارتداد والقصاص والرجم

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman cites the Prophet’s rule that Muslim blood is lawful only for a married adulterer, an intentional killer, or an apostate; he swears he committed none of these.
rows.anchor: وروى مطر الوراق عن نافع بن عمر عن عثمان رضي الله عنه أشرف على أصحابه وقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A guardian may approach an orphan’s property only for the orphan’s benefit and its growth.
rows.anchor: يعني بما فيه صلاحه وتثميره

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the best use of an orphan’s property is to trade with it.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو التجارة فيه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the guardian may invest the orphan’s property but may not take any of its profit.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أموال يبتغي له فيه ولا يأخذ من ربحه شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd permits a poor guardian to eat reasonably from the orphan’s property but requires a wealthy guardian to abstain.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: وأن يأكل بالمعروف إن افتقر، وإن استغنى لم يأكل

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi distinguishes necessary mixing to manage the orphan’s property from mixing only to consume it; the latter should be avoided until maturity.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: من خالط مال اليتيم حتى يفصل عليه فليخالطه

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Ya'mar says reaching الأشد means reaching puberty.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن يعمر: بلوغ الحلم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says الأشد is puberty, when good and bad deeds begin to be recorded.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: الأشد الحلم حيث يكتب له الحسنات وعليه السيئات

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says maturity comes when a person reasons well and has gathered strength.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: حتى يعقل ويجتمع قوته

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi defines الأشد as ages eighteen to thirty.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الأشد ما بين ثماني عشرة إلى ثلاثين سنة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says الأشد is thirty years, followed by the separate threshold of marriageable age.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: هو ثلاثون سنة ثم جاء بعدها حتى بلغوا النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأشد is the plural of شد and means a person’s full strength, youth, and age; شد النهار means the day’s height or middle.
rows.anchor: والأشد جمع شد، مثل قد وأقد، وهو استحكام قوما لفتى وشبابه وسنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fadl ibn Muhammad cites an Antara line using شد النهار for the height or intensity of daytime.
rows.anchor: [عهدي به] شد النهار كأنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching maturity does not permit using an orphan’s property except in the best way; once mature and prudent, the ward receives the property.
rows.anchor: وليس بلوغ الأشد مما يدع قرب ماله بغير الأحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfill measure and weight fairly; the capacity limit removes hardship from both seller and buyer, requiring the seller to give the due amount and the buyer to accept the due amount.
rows.anchor: لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها أي طاقتها في إيفاء الكيل والوزن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas warns non-Arabs that measure and weight were two causes of the destruction of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إنكم معشر الأعاجم فقد وليتم أمرين بهما هلك من كان قبلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When speaking, be truthful in judgment and testimony even about a relative; the omitted object is the person judged or testified against.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلتم فاعدلوا أي فاصدقوا في الحكم والشهادة ولو كان ذا قربى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says these clear commands were never abrogated, apply to all humanity, form the Mother of the Book, and lead their practitioners to Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا الآيات محكمات لم ينسخهن شيء في جميع الكتب

rows.speaker: كعب الأحبار
rows.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says the command beginning ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord forbade’ was the first thing in the Torah.
rows.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: والذي نفس كعب بيده إن هذا لأول شيء في التوراة

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khaytham recited these commands from a sealed sheet associated with Muhammad to his companions.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن خيثم لأصحابه: ألا أقرأ عليكم صحيفة عليها خاتم محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is God’s upright religion; the other paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, innovations, and misguidance that scatter people from the Prophet’s way.
rows.anchor: في هاتين الآيتين صراطي طريقي وديني مستقيما مستويا قويما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Then We gave Moses the Book’ may be phrased as an instruction to Muhammad because Moses received scripture before him; another view takes ثم to mean و.
rows.anchor: ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب يعني ثم قل يا محمد لهم آتينا موسى الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تماما is accusative as a specification; one reading of على الذي أحسن means completion for the doers of good, with الذي used collectively like من.
rows.anchor: تماما نصب على القطع، وقيل: على التفسير على الذي أحسن قال بعضهم: معناه تماما على المحسنين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reads على الذين أحسنوا in the plural, supporting the collective interpretation of the singular relative.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود (على الذين أحسنوا)

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd says God completed Moses’ quest with the Book and manifested its favor to the righteous, meaning prophets and believers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: معناه على كل من أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the Book a completion for the righteous and takes على to mean ‘for’; a further view reads الذي as ما, adding to Moses’ knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه: ثم آتينا موسى الكتاب متما للمحسنين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
rows.claim: Ibn Burayda interprets the phrase as completion from God’s favor to Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن بريدة: معناه تماما مني على مني وإحساني إلى موسى

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says it completes God’s beneficence and gifts to His prophets.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: معناه تماما على إحسان الله إلى أنبيائه وأياديه عندهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Book came as completion for the righteous among people, distinguishing them from wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: فمنهم المحسن ومنهم المسيء فنزل الكتاب تماما على المحسنين

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Ya'mar reads الذي أحسن with nominative رفع, meaning ‘the one who did good.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر: على الذي أحسن، بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book details the religious laws people need and offers guidance and mercy so they may believe in meeting their Lord.
rows.anchor: وتفصيلا بيانا لكل شيء يحتاج إليه من شرائع الدين وهدى ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed Book is the Qur'an; people should follow, practice, and obey it to receive mercy and avoid punishment.
rows.anchor: وهذا القرآن كتاب أنزلناه مبارك فاتبعوه واعملوا بما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians’ falsehoods are lies or distortions; when Moses’ sign swallowed their magic, they recognized that ropes and staffs would remain if it were mere magic.
rows.anchor: ما يأفكون يكذبون، وقيل: يقلبون ويزورون على الناس فأكلت سحرهم كله

rows.speaker: النضير بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Nadir ibn Shumayl glosses فوقع الحق as their being terrified and struck down; their magic failed and they were overcome and humiliated.
rows.anchor: قال النضير بن شميل: فوقع الحق أي فزعهم وصدعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers prostrated to God after recognizing a heavenly sign rather than magic; another view says God inspired them, and al-Akhfash says their rapid prostration made them seem thrown down.
rows.anchor: وألقي السحرة ساجدين لله حيث عرفوا أن ذلك أمر سماوي وليس سحرا

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the chief magicians were two brothers from distant Egyptian towns; they consulted their dead father, who told them a staff working while its owners slept would prove it divine.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: فكان رئيس السحرة بأقصى مدائن مصر وكانا أخوين

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says the staff turned toward the two brothers while they approached it secretly as Moses and Aaron slept.
rows.anchor: فقصدتهما العصا قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked the chief magician to believe if defeated; the magician pledged to believe if his magic were overcome, while Pharaoh called their faith a coordinated plot.
rows.anchor: قال موسى للساحر الأكبر: تؤمن بي إن غلبتك فقال لآتين بسحر لا يغلبه سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s threat means cutting limbs on opposite sides, then crucifying all of them on the bank of the Nile in Egypt.
rows.anchor: لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف وهو أن يقطع من شق طرفا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Pharaoh was the first to cut people’s limbs crosswise.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: أول من قطع من خلاف فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers tell Pharaoh that his only grievance against them is their belief in their Lord’s signs when they came to them.
rows.anchor: وما تنقم منا قرأ العامة بكسر القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says he will kill the Israelites’ sons repeatedly; the Hijaz readers use a lighter form of the verb, and he says he will dominate them.
rows.anchor: قال يعني فرعون سنقتل أبناءهم بالتشديد على التكثير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh killed Israelite boys in the predicted year, then ordered the killings resumed after Moses brought the message and the Israelites complained.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان فرعون يقتل بني إسرائيل في العام الذي قيل له إنه يولد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads يورثها with gemination; the author prefers the lighter reading because of the parallel ‘We made the earth an inheritance.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن يورثها بالتشديد والاختيار التخفيف لقوله تعالى وأورثنا الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome for the God-fearing is interpreted as victory and triumph, or alternatively felicity and martyrdom, or Paradise.
rows.anchor: والعاقبة للمتقين يعني النصر والظفر، وقيل: السعادة والشهادة، وقيل: الجنة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima, reporting from Ibn Abbas, says 600,000 Israelites followed Moses when the magicians believed; they describe oppression before and after his message.
rows.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: لما آمنت السحرة اتبع موسى ست مائة ألف

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb describes Israelite forced labor: heavy quarrying and stone hauling, brickmaking, carpentry, smithing, and taxes, with women spinning and weaving.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: كانوا أصنافا في أعمال فرعون فأما ذوو القوة منهم فيسلخون السوابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses tells the Israelites to seek God’s help and be patient because God owns Egypt and gives it to whichever servants He wills.
rows.anchor: فعند ذلك قال موسى لقومه استعينوا بالله واصبروا إن الأرض لله يعني أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised inheritance means Israelites will settle Egypt after Pharaoh’s people, including Egypt and Syria, blessed with water, trees, and fruit.
rows.anchor: ويسكنكم مصر من بعدهم بالتسخير والاستعباد وهم بنو إسرائيل مشارق الأرض ومغاربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن أحد من المشركين استجارك means ‘if one of the polytheists seeks your protection’; the wording is explained through Arabic usage and poetry.
rows.anchor: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك معناه وإن استجارك أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must shelter a hostile polytheist after the sacred months so he can hear God’s word and learn the proof and religion; if he converts he joins the Muslims, and if not he must be escorted safely home.
rows.anchor: فأجره فأعذه وأمنه حتى يسمع كلام الله فتقيم عليه حجة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the escorted person later fights and is captured, he may be killed; the reason given is that the polytheists do not know God’s religion and unity.
rows.anchor: فإن قاتلك بعد ذلك فقدرت عليه فاقتله ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعلمون دين الله وتوحيده

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the asylum command remains in force until the Day of Resurrection and has not been abrogated.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: وهذه الآية محكمة إلى يوم القيامة وليست بمنسوخة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says a polytheist asked Ali whether someone could come to Muhammad after the truce to hear him or meet a need; Ali answered yes and cited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: جاء رجل من المشركين إلى علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘How can the polytheists have a covenant?’ is a rhetorical question meaning they have no covenant, as an idiom that asserts its answer.
rows.anchor: كيف يكون للمشركين عهد عند الله وعند رسوله على [معنى] التعجب، ومعناه جحد

rows.speaker: ابن عياش
rows.claim: Ibn Ayyash identifies the people covenanted at the Sacred Mosque as Quraysh.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عياش: هم قريش

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd identify them as Meccans who made Hudaybiyya’s pact; after they broke it by aiding Banu Bakr, the Prophet gave them four months to choose Islam or departure, and they converted.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة وابن زيد: هم أهل مكة الذين عاهدهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الحديبية

rows.speaker: السدي وابن إسحاق والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, Ibn Ishaq, and al-Kalbi identify them as Banu Bakr groups allied to Quraysh; because only Quraysh and Banu al-Di'l broke the pact, the others’ treaty should stand to its term. The author calls this likelier because the verses followed the breach and conquest.
rows.anchor: قال السدي وابن إسحاق والكلبي: هم من قبائل بكر بن خزيمة وهو مدلج وبنو ضمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treaty-holders are those who did not break their agreement as Quraysh did or help Quraysh against the Prophet’s ally Khuza'a.
rows.anchor: فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم وإنما هم الذين قال الله عز وجل إلا الذين عاهدتم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses لا يرقبون as not preserving or respecting; in one gloss, الإل means kinship.
rows.anchor: لا يرقبوا قال ابن عباس: لا يحفظوا، وقال الأخفش: كيف لا يقتلونهم

rows.speaker: الأخفش، والضحاك، وقطرب
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the phrase as ‘how could they not kill you’; al-Dahhak says they do not wait, and Qutrub says they do not respect kinship.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: كيف لا يقتلونهم، وقال الضحاك: لا ينتظروا، وقال قطرب: لا يراعوا

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yaman says الإل means kinship, supported by Hassan’s line about Quraysh kinship.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان: رحما، دليله قول حسان: لعمرك إن إلك من قريش

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says الإل means an alliance or pact, supported by a line from Aws ibn Hajar.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الإل: الحلف، دليله قول أوس بن حجر:

rows.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd interpret الإل as a covenant; it is repeated as عهد despite the shared sense because the words differ, with poetry as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي وابن زيد: هو العهد، ولكنه لما اختلف الفظان كرر وإن كان معنا هما واحدا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One narration from Mujahid also takes الإل as a covenant, supported by a poetic line about a pact not being false.
rows.anchor: وهو إحدى الروايتين عن مجاهد يدل عليه قول الشاعر: وجدناهم كاذبا إلهم

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز ومجاهد
rows.claim: Abu Mijlaz and other reports from Mujahid say الإل means God; Ubayd ibn Umayr read Jibril emphatically, glossing it as servant of God, and Abu Bakr rejected Musaylima’s words as not from God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مجلز ومجاهد في ساير الروايات: الإل هو الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads إيلا with a yāʾ, meaning God, as in the names Jibril and Mika'il.
rows.anchor: والدليل على هذا التأويل قراءة عكرمة: لا يرقبون في مؤمن ايلا، بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذمة means a covenant or protection; alternatively it is reproach for those who lack a treaty. The polytheists make verbal promises contrary to their hearts, like hypocrites, and most are covenant-breakers.
rows.anchor: ولا ذمة عهدا وجمعها ذمم، وقيل: تذمما ممن لا عهد له يرضونكم بأفواههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sold God’s signs for a small price by breaking their covenant after Abu Sufyan fed and supported them.
rows.anchor: اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا وذلك أنهم نقضوا العهد الذي بينهم وبين الرسول

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Abu Sufyan fed his own alliance and abandoned Muhammad’s alliance, so they blocked people from Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أطعم أبو سفيان حلفا وترك حلف محمد

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says Abu Sufyan supplied camels and food to keep people from following the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء كان أبو سفيان يعطي الناقة والطعام ليصد الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people of Ta'if gave them money to strengthen them for war against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وذلك أن أهل الطائف أمدوهم بالأموال ليقووهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are told not to spare the treaty-breakers, since they would show believers no mercy if victorious; their aggression is their breach of covenant.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تبقوا عليهم أيها المؤمنون كما لا يبقون عليكم لو ظهروا عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent from shirk, pray, and pay zakat become religious brothers with the same rights and duties; the verses are explained to the knowledgeable.
rows.anchor: فإخوانكم يعني فهم إخوانكم في الدين لهم ما لكم وعليهم ما عليكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this verse made the blood of the people of the qibla inviolable.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حرمت هذه الآية دماء أهل القبلة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says prayer and zakat were prescribed together; he would not accept prayer without zakat and praises Abu Bakr’s understanding.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: افترض الصلاة والزكاة جميعا ولم يفرق بينهما

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says people were commanded to pray and give zakat, and one who does not give zakat has no prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: أمرتم بالصلاة والزكاة فمن لم يزك لا صلاة له

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Suhayb reports that the people of Paradise will see God after the veil is lifted, and that nothing they receive will be more beloved to them.
rows.anchor: عن صهيب قال: قال: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا دخل أهل الجنة الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says those who do good and receive the best are those who testify that there is no god but God and enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الذين أحسنوا الحسنى يعني الذين شهدوا أن لا إله إلا الله الجنة

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: Atiyya, reporting from Ibn Abbas, says the good deed is rewarded once and the increase multiplies it from tenfold to seven hundredfold.
rows.anchor: وروى عطية عنه هي أن واحدة من الحسنات واحدة والزيادة التضعيف بعشر أمثالها

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit says the best reward is the vision and the increase is seeing God, citing the description of faces looking toward their Lord.
rows.anchor: وروى جويبر عن الليث عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط قال: الحسنى: النظرة، والزيادة: النظر

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says the increase is a single pearl chamber with four thousand doors.
rows.anchor: وروى الحكم عن علي بن أبي طالب (رضي الله عنه) قال: الزيادة غرفة من لؤلؤ واحدة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the good reward is one good deed for one, while the increase is God’s forgiveness and approval.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: الحسنى: حسنة مثل حسنة والزيادة مغفرة من الله ورضوان

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the best reward is Paradise; the increase is whatever God grants them in prayer without reckoning on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: الحسنى: الجنة والزيادة ما أعطاهم في الدعاء لا يحاسبهم به يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: يزيد بن شجرة
rows.claim: Yazid ibn Shajara says a cloud passes over the people of Paradise, asks what they want, and rains any delights they choose.
rows.anchor: حكى منصور بن عمار عن يزيد بن شجرة قال: الزيادة: هي أن تمر السحابة بأهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قتر is dust that covers faces; Ibn Abbas and Qatada instead gloss it as blackness, while Hasan reads قتر with a still t, a dialectal variant like قدر and قدر.
rows.anchor: ولا يرهق يغشى ويلحق وجوههم قتر غبار وهو جمع قترة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the absence of humiliation as absence of gloom and eclipse from the faces.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: سواد الوجوه، وقرأ الحسن: قتر بسكون التاء وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Layla says this scene of security follows the believers’ vision of their Lord.
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي ليلى: هذا بعد نظرهم إلى ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase جزاء سيئة بمثلها can be parsed as an omitted predicate meaning ‘they have a recompense’, or as an initial clause with مثلها explained by an added باء.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون الجزاء مرفوعا بإضمار أي: لهم جزاء

rows.speaker: الأعرج
rows.claim: Al-A'raj reads كلمات على الذين فسقوا كفروا أنهم لا يؤمنون.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج: كلمات على الذين فسقوا كفروا أنهم لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the partners originated creation without a model and then restore it after death; if they cannot answer, Muhammad should say God originates and restores creation.
rows.anchor: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدؤا الخلق ينشئ من غير أصل ولا [مثال] ثم يعيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فأنى تؤفكون means ‘how are you turned away’ from the straight path.
rows.anchor: فأنى تؤفكون تصرفون عن قصد السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the idols cannot guide to truth, people must acknowledge that God guides to it and is more deserving of being followed than one who cannot guide without guidance.
rows.anchor: قل هل من شركائكم أوثانكم من يهدي يرشد إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readers differ on يهدي: Medinans have a jussive silent hāʾ with geminated dāl from assimilation; Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir use a fatḥa, preferred by Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim; Asim and Warsh use kasra.
rows.anchor: اختلف القراء فيه، فقرأ أهل المدينة: مجزومة الهاء مشددة الدال

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Adam transmits from Abu Bakr from Asim a reading with kasra on both hāʾ and yāʾ and a geminated dāl; Abu Amr reads between fatḥ and jazm, while Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf use a light dāl meaning يَهتدي.
rows.anchor: وروى يحيى ابن آدم عن أبي بكر عن عاصم بكسر الهاء والياء وتشديد الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading may refer to leaders and misleaders who do not guide unless guided, or to idols that cannot move unless carried; a line illustrates being carried by one’s feet.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يهدى في معنى الآية وجهان: فصرفها قوم إلى الرؤساء والمظلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people follow conjecture that idols are gods and will intercede; conjecture cannot replace truth, and God knows what they do.
rows.anchor: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا منهم إنها آلهة وأنها تشفع لهم في الآخرة وأراد بالأكثر الكل إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas tells how Joseph later recognized his brothers while they did not recognize him; his cup identified their past betrayal, including throwing him in a well and lying to their father.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما دخل إخوة يوسف على يوسف فعرفهم وهم له منكرون دعا بالصواع

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the brothers beat Joseph in the wilderness; Judah stopped them from killing him because they had pledged their father, and they cast him into a well.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: أرسل يعقوب يوسف معهم فأخرجوه وبه عليهم من الكرامة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The brothers removed Joseph’s shirt, mocked his request for it, and threw him into the well; after he answered their call, Judah prevented them from crushing him with a rock.
rows.anchor: فقال: يا إخوتاه، ردوا علي القميص أتوارى به في الجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says God raised a rock beneath Joseph in the well; Gabriel then clothed him in the heavenly shirt inherited by Isaac and Jacob from Abraham and kept as Joseph’s amulet.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن الله تعالى أمر صخرة حتى ارتفعت من أسفل البئر فوقف يوسف عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the brothers slaughtered a young sheep and smeared its blood on Joseph’s shirt.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثم ذبحوا سخلة وجعلوا دمها على قميص يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers came at night weeping to make their false excuse easier to present; another explanation says they delayed until evening to deceive Jacob.
rows.anchor: وجاؤ أباهم عشاء يبكون ليكونوا أجرأ في الظلمة على الاعتذار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Jacob heard them and feared something had happened to them or their sheep, then asked where Joseph was.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: فلما سمع أصواتهم فزع وقال: ما لكم يا بنى؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نستبق is glossed as throwing at one another, supported by Abdullah’s reading ننتضل; al-Suddi and Ibn Hayyan instead say ‘we raced.’
rows.anchor: قالوا يا أبانا إنا ذهبنا نستبق أي نترامى، دليله قول عبد الله: ننتضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say Joseph was left with their baggage and eaten by a wolf; they expect Jacob not to believe them even if truthful because he suspects them.
rows.anchor: وما أنت بمؤمن مصدق لنا ولو كنا صادقين لسوء ظنك بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blood on the shirt was false because it was sheep’s blood, not Joseph’s; alternatively the phrase means blood that was lied about or ‘a blood of lying.’
rows.anchor: وجاؤ على قميصه بدم كذب أي بدم كذب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha read كدب with a dal, meaning fresh blood.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عائشة: بدم كدب بالدال غير المعجمة، أي طري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob points out that the wolf supposedly ate Joseph without tearing his shirt, calling it a remarkably judicious wolf.
rows.anchor: فقال: يا لله ما رأيت كاليوم ذئبا أحلم من هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل سولت لكم means the brothers’ own selves arranged a plan; فصبر جميل may mean my state or act is beautiful patience, or simply ‘my patience is beautiful.’
rows.anchor: فحينئذ قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم رتبت لكم أمرا فصبر أي فمني أو فعلي صبر

rows.speaker: الأشهب والعقيلي
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab and al-Uqayli read فصبرا as an accusative verbal noun, meaning ‘I will be patient’ with no lament or complaint.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب والعقيلي: فصبرا على المصدر أي فلأصبرن صبرا جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Jacob will continue to deal with his sons graciously rather than in a mournful, grieving manner.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا أعاشركم على كآبة الوجه وحبوس الحنين، بل أكون في المعاشرة

rows.speaker: حبيب بن ثابت
rows.claim: A report says Jacob’s brows drooped over his eyes from long years and sorrow; God asked if he complained of Him, and Jacob asked forgiveness for a sin.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الرزاق عن الثوري عن حبيب بن ثابت أن يعقوب النبي (عليه السلام) كان قد سقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says God is the help against the brothers’ false account; reports place Joseph’s age when thrown in the well at eighteen, seventeen, or ten, and his stay there at three days.
rows.anchor: والله المستعان على ما تصفون من الكذب، قالوا: وكان يوسف حين ألقي في الجب ابن ثماني عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun and moon persist in their regular course in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: دؤوبهما في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are subjected by alternating light and darkness and by their increase and decrease.
rows.anchor: وسخر لكم الليل والنهار متعاقبان في الضياء والظلمة والنقصان والزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He gave you of all you asked’ may omit a second شيء: you receive something from each category requested; another reading treats ‘all’ as general abundance rather than literal totality.
rows.anchor: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه يعني وآتاكم من كل شيء سألتموه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God granted both what people asked for and what they never asked for; the common reading attaches ما سألتموه in an إضافة construction.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: معناه وآتاه من كل ما سألتموه وما لم تسألوه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says God gave people things they did not request or even imagine, as the speaker can attest.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: أعطاكم أشياء ما طلبتموها ولا سألتموها

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وسلام
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Salam read من كل with nunation, construing the phrase as provision from what people had not asked for.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والضحاك وسلام: من كل، بالتنوين على النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot enumerate God’s blessings or fulfill their thanks for them by heart, tongue, or explanation.
rows.anchor: ولا القيام بشركها لا بالجنان ولا باللسان ولا بالبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is unjust by failing to thank a benefactor and placing gratitude wrongly, and ungrateful by denying God’s blessings; other views tie injustice to disobedience or hardship and ingratitude to hoarding in prosperity.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان لظلوم لشاكر غير من أنعم عليه واضع الشكر في غير موضعه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports the Prophet saying Moses’ sandals were made from the hide of a dead donkey; another report says the hide was untanned.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله فاخلع نعليك قال: كانتا من جلد حمار ميت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan answers why Moses removed his sandals although Muhammad prayed in sandals: Moses’ sandals were made from donkey hide.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما بال خلع النعلين في الصلاة وصلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في نعليه؟

rows.speaker: أبو الأحوص
rows.claim: Abu al-Ahwas recounts Ibn Mas'ud yielding the prayer lead to Abu Musa, who removed his sandals; Ibn Mas'ud joked, ‘Are you in the sacred valley?’
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الأحوص: أتى عبد الله أبا موسى في داره فأقيمت الصلاة

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid say Moses removed his sandals so his feet touched the blessed earth and received its blessing, sanctified twice.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومجاهد: إنما قال له: اخلع نعليك كي تمس راحة قدميك الأرض الطيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say barefootedness marks humility, allows the heels to receive the valley’s blessing, or symbolizes emptying one’s heart of family and children; shoes in dreams signify a wife.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أمر بذلك لأن الحفوة من أمارات التواضع

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Tuwa is a circular, deep valley; other interpretations relate the name to traversing the valley, night, or blessing folded into it.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: مستدير عميق مثل الطوى في استدارته

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads طوى with kasra on the ṭāʾ; the text says the form has two dialectal readings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة: طوى بكسر الطاء وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan and Syrian readers use tanwin and genitive inflection; others omit tanwin because the word is a diptote derived from طاو or مطوي.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة والشام: طوى بالتنوين وإلا جرا لتذكيره وتحقيقه

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads ‘We have chosen you’ in the plural of majesty; اخترتك means ‘I selected you.’
rows.anchor: وأنا اخترتك اصطفيتك، وقرأ حمزة: وإنا اخترناك بلفظ الجمع على التعظيم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says establish prayer so that you remember God within it.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: أقم الصلاة لتذكرني فيها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says that if one misses prayer, one should perform it when one remembers it.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: إذا تركت الصلاة ثم ذكرتها فأقمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses used the staff to shake leaves from trees for his sheep to eat.
rows.anchor: وأهش وأخبط بها الشجر ليتناثر ورقها فتأكل غنمي

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl recounts al-Khalil’s explanation that Arabic often substitutes sīn for shīn, as in examples for sneezing, armor, and a seal.
rows.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: سألت الخليل عن قراءة عكرمة فقال: العرب تعاقب بين الشين والسين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses’ staff carried food and water, produced them, herded and guarded sheep, fought attackers, drew water from wells, lit his way at night, and grew fruit trees on demand.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان موسى عليه السلام يحمل عليها زاده وسقاءه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the serpent first as a yellow, horse-crested snake that swelled into a dragon; one reading distinguishes the small initial state from the large final state.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: صارت حية صفراء لها عرف كعرف الفرس

rows.speaker: فرقد السخي
rows.claim: Farqad al-Sakhi says the serpent’s width between its flanks was forty cubits.
rows.anchor: قال فرقد السخي: كان ما بين جنبيها أربعين ذراعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reassures Moses and says He will return the serpent to its former form as a staff.
rows.anchor: سنُعيدها سيرتها أي إلى سيرتها وهيئتها الأولى

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads وأهس with sīn, meaning ‘I drive away the sheep’; Arabic often alternates sīn and shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة «وأهس» بالسين يعني وازجر بها الغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مآرب means needs or uses; its singular has two vowel forms, and the plural أخر is avoided to preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: ولي فيها مآرب حوائج ومنافع، واحدتها مأربة ومأربة بفتح الراء وضمها أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word حية can encompass small and large, male and female snakes.
rows.anchor: فأما الحية فإنها تجمع الصغر والكبر والذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi locates the hand below the armpit; Mujahid says under the arm, and Maqatil glosses the phrase as with the upper arm.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: أسفل من الإبط، وقال مجاهد: تحت عضدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ hand emerges white without leprosy or disease, a second sign beyond the staff; its radiance resembles the sun and dazzles the eye.
rows.anchor: تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء برص ولا داء آية أخرى سوى العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine الكبرى may match the verse ending; alternatively an omitted noun means ‘the greatest sign,’ as Ibn Abbas says Moses’ hand was his greatest sign.
rows.anchor: وكان من حقه الكبر وإنما قال: الكبرى وفاقا لرءوس الآي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses’ hand was his greatest sign.
rows.anchor: دليله قول ابن عباس: كانت يد موسى أكبر آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Thamud? The passage identifies the people of the thicket as Shu'ayb’s people; al-Ayka and al-Layka are two dialectal forms, both read in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: كذب أصحاب الأيكة الغيضة وهم قوم شعيب والليكة والأيكة لغتان

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd says God sent Shu'ayb to his own people of Midian and also to the nomadic people of the thicket.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد : بعث الله سبحانه شعيبا إلى قومه وأهل مدين وإلى أهل البادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not call Shu'ayb their brother because he was not genealogically one of the thicket people; it does call him Midian’s brother because he belonged to them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم شعيب لأنه لم يكن من أصحاب الأيكة في النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets’ repeated call to fear and obey God, worship sincerely, and seek no payment shows that their truth is one and their message is shared.
rows.anchor: وإنما دعوة هؤلاء الأنبياء كلهم فيما حكى الله سبحانه عنهم على صيغة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أوفوا الكيل means give full measure and do not reduce people’s measures or weights.
rows.anchor: أوفوا الكيل ولا تكونوا من المخسرين الناقصين للكيل والوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: القسطاس المستقيم means the just, straight balance; do not diminish people’s goods or spread corruption.
rows.anchor: وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الجبلة means created beings or creatures; a poetic line supports the lexical gloss.
rows.anchor: والجبلة الخليقة الأولين. والجبل: الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shu'ayb answers that God knows what his opponents do and will requite them; his duty is only to deliver the message.
rows.anchor: قال ربي أعلم بما تعملون وهو مجازيكم به وما علي إلا الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the thicket were denied shade and suffered seven days of heat; a cloud offered coolness, drew them beneath it, then rained fire and burned them.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الله سبحانه حبس عنهم الريح سبعة أيام وسلط عليهم الحر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Shu'ayb was sent to two peoples: the thicket people died by the shade punishment, while Midian was destroyed by Gabriel’s cry.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: بعث الله سبحانه شعيبا إلى أمتين: أصحاب الأيكة وأهل مدين

rows.speaker: برد الجريري
rows.claim: Bard al-Jariri reports that after seven days and nights of heat, a distant mountain appeared with cool water; after everyone gathered beneath it, it fell on them.
rows.anchor: عن برد الجريري قال: سلط الحر عليهم سبعة أيام ولياليهن، ثم رفع لهم جبل من بعيد
